Accountable for patient outcomes resulting from the nursing care for the patient undergoing a surgical/ invasive procedure.

The perioperative OR RN plans, directs and coordinates the care of every patient undergoing operative and other invasive procedures, taking into consideration respect for the individual and recognition of the important contribution that each team member makes to the patient's well-being.

This OR RN is expected to function proficiently in both the circulator and scrub role within the OR and to be competent in all surgical specialties served. The OR RN maintains knowledge of current Association of peri-Operative Registered Nurses (AORN) Standards, VHA Directives, and service level standard operating procedures.

The OR RN assures the sterility of the surgical field is maintained and all instrumentation and equipment in play is used in a safe and efficient manner.

The OR RN protects the patient from injury caused by chemical, electrical, mechanical, and thermal sources, and extraneous objects, performs counting procedures to protect the patient from unintended retained surgical items, participates in the Time Out process to ensure correct site, side, and level, and follow implant and tissue/tissue-based product documentation, policy, and procedures.

The OR RN manages the patient's specimens in the appropriate manner, administers medications safely and correctly, performs interventions to maintain the patient's wound and tissue perfusion at or above baseline levels, and performs interventions to protect the patient from surgical site infection.

The OR RN is responsible for ensuring comprehensive documentation of all care provided during the perioperative experience is timely, complete, and accurate in the electronic health record. The OR RN is required to be on-call during off tours hours to provide patient care for emergency procedures.

This position requires visual acuity, keen hearing, clear distinctive speech, and manual dexterity. This position may require potentially long periods of continued walking, standing, stooping, sitting, bending, pulling, and pushing. Transferring patients and objects may be required.

The Nurse may be exposed to infected patients and contaminated materials and maybe required to don protective clothing in isolation situations or operative/invasive procedures. The Nurse may occasionally be exposed to patients who are combative secondary to delirium, dementia, or psychotic disorders.

The Nurse must be a mature, flexible, sensible, individual capable of working effectively in stressful situations, able to shift priorities based on patient care and unit needs. The Nurse must also meet Employee Health requirements as a condition of employment.

The Nurse Post Anesthesia Care Unit (PACU) Registered Nurse (RN) provides specialized care in the assessment, planning, implementing and evaluation of care throughout the peri anesthesia continuum to include the Pre anesthesia Phase, Post anesthesia Phase I, Post anesthesia Phase II, and extended care from sedation/analgesia and/or anesthesia for surgical, diagnostic, or therapeutic procedures.

The PACU RN possesses knowledge related to the physiology associated with various anesthesia techniques and surgical interventions. The PACU RN assesses and prepare patients for procedures appropriately. Performs clinical assessment of the patient and readily recognizes contraindication for anesthesia and/or surgical intervention.

The PACU RN applies the appropriate post sedation scoring and assesses the patient's postoperative status to include cardiovascular and respiratory systems and airway management needs, neurological system, hemodynamic stability, pain, and comfort needs and mental status, implementing appropriate interventions to maintain or return all physiological system to baseline or above.

The PACU RN maintains knowledge of current American Society of Peri anesthesia Nurses (ASPAN) standards, Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Directives and service level standard operating procedures (SOPs).

The PACU RN is responsible for ensuring comprehensive documenting of all phases of care and is timely, complete, and accurate in the electronic health record (EHR). Other duties as assigned Work Schedule: 0900-1730 Preferred Qualifications 2-5 years of recent PACU experience in an acute-care hospital setting. ACLS and BLS certifications

Duties The Nursing, GEC Nurse Manager (NM) is a registered professional nurse Responsible for the assessment, planning, provision and evaluation of nursing care on inpatient and outpatient services. NM provides 24/7 responsibility and accountability including weekends, and holidays.

Responsible and accountable for the management and supervision of all nursing staff personnel on all tours of duty.

Executes position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches to management of complex client Responsible for directing and organizing the unit specific orientation, training and development of staff and for directing, supervising, and evaluating their performance.

Accountable for the provision of direct patient care and for the delivery of quality nursing care during times when the unit staffing is low and necessary to provide safe care to the veterans. Functions as nursing role model, educator, practitioner and manager, providing leadership to an interdisciplinary team.

Demonstrates the knowledge and skills necessary to provide care appropriate to the age-related needs of patients served in the assigned area of practice. This knowledge includes understanding changes associated with aging and principles of growth and development relevant to the adult and geriatric population.

Responsible for providing leadership in delivering and improving care through the collaboration with others. May receive a variety of additional assignments or special projects to either meet the needs of the Medical Center or designed for the growth of the individual.

Accountable and responsible for possessing the knowledge and skill to communicate and interact appropriately and courteously with all internal and external customers. Will maintain confidentiality of electronic, written and verbal patient/employee information.

Demonstrate working practices that include adherence to infection control standards and the safe use and operation of equipment. The NM will treat customers in a courteous and helpful manner that indicates dignity and respect. Will respond to customer requests in a timely manner.

Will be courteous, thoughtful, and caring in all interactions with patients, family members, visitors, and staff. Will use tact, discretion and patience when explaining policies and procedures and/or when assisting in finding an answer to a problem.

Displays a helpful, proactive attitude toward customers by answering questions and resolving problems to enhance customer satisfaction. Accepts assignments willingly, volunteers to help others, and works cooperatively and effectively with co-workers and supervisors displaying a helpful, positive attitude.

Consistently practices customer service performance expectations consistent with VHA ICARE values. All other duties as assigned. Functions as a clinical expert and is responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing or supervising direct patient care.

Assesses, plans, implements, and evaluates delivery of care based on age specific components. Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction throughout the continuum of care.

Dipl. Pflegefachperson HF/FH 40-50% Flexpool Wochenende - Einsätze im Frühdienst
**Flexibel arbeiten. Verlässlich pflegen. Wochenenden selbst wählen.**
Du möchtest deine pflegerische Fachkompetenz gezielt am Wochenende einsetzen und selbst bestimmen, an welchen Wochenenden du arbeitest? In unserem Flexpool übernimmst du ausschliesslich Frühdienste am Wochenende. Deine Einsätze planst du im vereinbarten Pensum von 40-50 % flexibel und passend zu deiner persönlichen Situation.
**Deine Aufgaben**
· Du pflegst und begleitest unsere Klientinnen und Klienten selbstständig in ihrem Zuhause.
· Du übernimmst am Wochenende Einsätze ausschliesslich im Frühdienst.
· Du führst pflegerische und medizinaltechnische Massnahmen fachgerecht durch.
· Du beobachtest Veränderungen im Gesundheitszustand und leitest die notwendigen Schritte ein.
· Du stellst eine vollständige Pflegedokumentation und einen verlässlichen Informationsfluss sicher.
**Das bringst du mit**
· Diplom als Pflegefachperson HF/FH oder eine gleichwertige, in der Schweiz anerkannte Ausbildung
· Berufserfahrung als diplomierte Pflegefachperson, idealerweise in der ambulanten Pflege
· Selbstständige, verantwortungsbewusste und strukturierte Arbeitsweise
· Hohe Sozialkompetenz und Freude an der Begleitung von Menschen in ihrem Zuhause
· Sicherer Umgang mit digitalen Arbeitsmitteln und Führerausweis Kategorie B
**Darauf kannst du dich freuen**
**Frei wählbare Wochenenden**
Du gibst deine Verfügbarkeiten an und entscheidest im Rahmen der Einsatzplanung selbst, an welchen Wochenenden du arbeitest.
**Ausschliesslich Frühdienst**
Deine Einsätze finden am Wochenende nur im Frühdienst statt.
**Flexpool mit Planungssicherheit**
Du arbeitest in einem vereinbarten Pensum von 40-50 % und kannst deine Einsätze frühzeitig planen.
**Verantwortung und Teamunterstützung**
Du arbeitest selbstständig und kannst dich auf klare Abläufe sowie verlässliche Ansprechpersonen verlassen.
**Zeitgemässe Arbeitsbedingungen**
Moderne digitale Arbeitsmittel und attraktive Anstellungsbedingungen unterstützen dich im Arbeitsalltag.
**Was uns ausmacht**
Wir verbinden professionelle ambulante Pflege mit flexiblen Arbeitsmodellen. Im Flexpool kannst du deine Wochenenden passend zu deinem Alltag planen und gleichzeitig einen wichtigen Beitrag zur verlässlichen Versorgung unserer Klientinnen und Klienten leisten.

## Company Description ##
Avec plus de 13'000 collaborateurs et collaboratrices représentant 160 métiers, les Hôpitaux Universitaires de Genève sont un établissement de référence au niveau national et international. Pour en savoir plus sur notre institution, prenez quelques minutes pour consulter notre rétrospective 2025 en cliquant ici.
Le Département de médecine de premier recours (DMPR) a pour mission sociétale de permettre un accès aux soins de qualité pour tous par une médecine de proximité, d-assurer la prise en charge des urgences médicales et chirurgicales légères, de promouvoir la prévention auprès des citoyennes et citoyens, d-apporter les connaissances médicales aux investigations judiciaires et de promouvoir la santé des voyageurs et voyageuses.
Le service de médecine tropicale et humanitaire assure la prise en charge de patients ayant voyagé et présentant une pathologie d-importation, tropicale ou parasitaire et prodigue des conseils de prévention. Il effectue des vaccinations spécialisées pour les voyageurs, les expatriés, les étudiants et la population locale. Par ailleurs, ce service participe activement aux interventions vaccinales en cas d-épidémie ou autre besoin identifié.
## Job Description ##
En qualité d-infirmier ou infirmière au Service de médecine tropicale et humanitaire (SMTH), votre mission consiste à mener de manière autonome des consultations infirmières de pré-voyage auprès d-une patientèle très diversifiée (expatriés, familles, humanitaires, immunosupprimés).
Vous menez et gérez des consultations infirmières de première ligne de manière autonome, dans le respect des missions, des protocoles et des délégations qui vous sont confiés.
Vous assurez également une activité de conseil aux voyageurs et voyageuses en formulant des recommandations personnalisées en matière de prévention des risques liés au voyage (vaccinations, prophylaxie, mesures d-hygiène, prévention des maladies infectieuses et autres risques sanitaires). Vous participez activement aux campagnes de vaccinations sur différents sites.
Vous travaillez en collaboration avec une équipe pluriprofessionnelle ainsi qu-avec les réseaux de soins internes et externes, notamment les organisations non gouvernementales, les organisations internationales et les partenaires présents au Global Health Campus.
Votre empathie, votre sens du relationnel et votre capacité à créer un climat de confiance vous permettent de vous positionner comme un partenaire de soins à part entière.
Doté ou dotée d-une excellente capacité d-adaptation et de l-organisation, vous êtes en mesure de faire face à des flux de patients importants et variables tout en maintenant une prise en charge de qualité. Vous gérez sereinement les imprévus et les situations génératrices de stress.
Vous possédez d-excellentes compétences relationnelles, un sens développé d l-accueil et une communication bienveillante, vous permettant de répondre aux attentes d-une patientèle exigeante et multiculturelle.
Dans le cadre de votre activité, vous êtes amené ou amenée à intervenir sur deux sites.

Vous possédez un Bachelor HES en soins infirmiers ou un diplôme en soins infirmiers équivalent reconnu par la Croix-Rouge suisse.
Vous avez une pratique professionnelle diversifiée de plus de 4 ans dans le domaine de la santé publique et/ou en santé communautaire et des connaissances en vaccinologie. Vous êtes au bénéfice d-une formation à l-évaluation clinique infirmière.
Une formation en médecine tropicale et des voyageurs constitue un réel atout.
Vous disposez d-un très bon niveau d-anglais, tant à l-oral qu-à l-écrit. La maitrise d-une autre langue, constitue un atout.
Vous savez vous adapter à divers contextes, aux imprévus, aux variations de charge de travail.
Vous possédez d-excellentes compétences relationnelles, un sens de l-accueil d-une communication bienveillante.

Major Duties: The Nurse V Associate Director for Patient Care Service (ADPCS) is an advanced healthcare executive who executes responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches in the guidance and direction of a variety of complex patient care services and programs.

The Nurse V DADPCS is of an executive nature, comprised of complex leadership and administrative components associated with critical health care issues and activities that influence the organizational mission, health care, and policy. hey are accountable to the Health Care System Medical Director and are an integral part of the senior leadership team.

The ADPCS is a member of the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and is the top executive within nursing services.

The incumbent is the chief spokesperson for organized nursing services and is the catalyst for the integration and collaboration of nursing with other professional disciplines and functional areas in the mutual achievement of optimal Veteran centered organizational goals.

The ADPCS is a key leader in strategic planning, organization assessment, and program development. The ADPCS participates with the ELT and strategic thought leaders in the facility to initiate and execute planning and decision-making processes.

They have the authority and responsibility for establishing standards for the practice of nursing at the health care system level ensuring the continuous and timely availability of quality nursing services. The ADPCS is responsible for the practice of nursing 24/7.

This includes all registered nurses, advanced practice nurses, and allied health staff (LPNs, NAs, etc.) regardless of line authority. They have line authority over the Deputy Associate Director Patient Care Services (DADPCS), Sterile Processing Service (SPS), and Social Work Service (SWS).

The incumbent exercises final authority and approval for the following: job descriptions, policies, and procedures; standards of patient care, treatment, and services; nursing practice standards; staffing plans; functional statements; and standards to measure, assess, and improve patient outcomes.

Appropriately delegates activities to those service lines under the purview of the ADPCS. They ensure all registered nurses, advanced practice nurses, and licensed practical/vocational nurses are licensed, certified, and/or registered upon employment, and thereafter.

The ADPCS ensures a competency process is in place to evaluate individual practice, as well as a review process for annual performance ratings.

The ADPCS promotes a healthy work environment for nursing through the implementation of shared decision-making; a spirit of inquiry and the use of evidence-based practice; and an academic environment supportive of education and research to promote the profession of nursing.

Champions a High Reliability Organization (HRO) founded on a collective mindfulness approach to develop evidence-based health care solutions that promote a culture of prevention and safety. Establishes the strategic direction for health care delivery, evidence-based practices, industry-leading research, and innovative care models.

Creates a shared vision and successfully leads change to improve performance and attain measurable outcomes at the organization or enterprise level. Transforms established practices to cultivate a culture of inquiry/innovation for the future.

VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards Pay: Competitive salary, regular salary increases, potential for performance awards Paid Time Off: 50 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory Work Schedule: M-F 8:00 to 4:30 Telework: Ad-hoc
Basic Requirements: English Language Proficiency. In accordance with 38 U.S.C. 7403(f), no person shall serve in direct patient care positions unless they are proficient in basic written and spoken English.

Graduate of a school of professional nursing approved by the appropriate accrediting agency and accredited by one of the following accrediting bodies at the time the program was completed by the applicant: The Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN) or The Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE); OR Individuals attending a master's level bridge program in nursing who have completed coursework equivalent to a bachelor's level degree in Nursing may have opportunity to become registered as a nurse with a state licensing board prior to completion of the bridge program.

Upon achievement of a State license, the individual may be appointed on temporary basis and later converted to a permanent appointment upon successful completion and graduation from the bridge program.

(Reference VA Handbook 5005, Appendix G6); OR In cases of graduates of foreign schools of professional nursing, possession of a current, full, active, and unrestricted registration will meet the requirement for graduation from an approved school of professional nursing to warrant an appointment as a Nurse who has completed an associated degree/entry level Nursing education program.

Credit for foreign nursing education higher that associate degree/entry level requires a formal degree equivalency validation from a recognized equivalency evaluation accepted by VA such as International Consultants of Delaware (ICD).

Current, full, active, and unrestricted registration as a graduate professional nurse in a State, Territory or Commonwealth (i.e., Puerto Rico) of the United States, or the District of Columbia.

Graduate Nurse Technician (GNT) Exception: Candidates who otherwise meet the basic education requirements, but do not possess the required licensure, may be appointed at the entry step of the grade and level applicable to the completed nursing education as a GNT on a 120-day temporary appointment while actively pursuing licensure (may be extended up to two years on a case-by-case-basis.) Assistant Nurse Manager (ANM) in the Primary Care Mental Health Integration (PCMHI) program, you play a vital role in supporting clinical operations, fostering evidence-based practice, and ensuring high-quality, recovery-oriented care for Veterans.

This position requires you to dedicate 50% of your time to direct clinical patient care, while also providing leadership and guidance to PCMHI nursing staff. Your collaborative approach enhances care coordination between primary care and mental health teams, maintains standards, and supports ongoing program development.

Key responsibilities include: Provide direct clinical supervision to PCMHI nursing staff. Coordinate daily operations and patient assignments within PCMHI. Conduct performance evaluations and support professional growth. Lead care coordination efforts across primary care and mental health services.

Promote and apply evidence-based mental health interventions. Monitor patient safety and protocol adherence. Participate in quality improvement initiatives. Support training, orientation, and ongoing PCMHI nursing education. Ensure accurate and timely completion of CPRS documentation. Serve as a liaison for interdisciplinary communication.

Address operational challenges and escalate issues as needed. Maintain awareness of resources and report supply needs. Enforce adherence to facility, VA, and regulatory policies. Foster a recovery-oriented environment for patient engagement. Support the growth and enhancement of PCMHI programs and services.

Deals effectively with employee conduct and performance issues, completing disciplinary action where appropriate and/or necessary. Addresses and resolves complaints from and/or of employee members as able or appropriately referring more serious complaints. Completes and updates competencies for staff education to relevant and pertinent skills.

Addresses patient complaints/concerns which may include collaboration with Patient Advocacy Services to complete required investigations and ensure appropriate resolution. Leads and participates in service level and medical center committees. Leads unit based huddles and disseminates information timely to employees.

Provide direct clinical patient care for 50% of assigned duties. Embody and promote VA ICARE Values: Integrity, Commitment, Advocacy, Respect, and Excellence in all interactions and decision-making. Uphold and advance the values, mission, and vision specific to VA San Diego ensuring alignment with organizational goals and priorities.

Perform other duties as assigned by the Nurse Manager, IU3 Co-Section Chiefs, Service Chief and/or Chief Nurse, Mental Health.

VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards Pay: Competitive salary, regular salary increases, potential for performance awards Paid Time Off: 50 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory Work Schedule: M-F, 0700-1700 Telework: Not Available Virtual: This is not a virtual position.

Pflege, die Wirkung zeigt. Dort, wo Menschen am liebsten sind: zu Hause. Jeden Tag begleiten wir Menschen in ihrer vertrauten Umgebung.
Eine ältere Klientin, die trotz Krankheit in ihrem vertrauten Zuhause bleiben möchte. Ein jüngerer Klient, der nach dem Spitalaufenthalt Schritt für Schritt Sicherheit zurückgewinnt. Eine Familie, die in einer herausfordernden Situation kompetente Unterstützung erhält und wieder etwas durchatmen kann.
Und Sie mittendrin: Sie sind da, wenn Pflege mehr bedeutet als Versorgung. Mit Fachkompetenz und Empathie übernehmen Sie Verantwortung.
Bei Spitex Nidwalden sind rund 160 Fachkräfte für Gesundheit, Pflege und Hauswirtschaft täglich unterwegs. Gemeinsam ermöglichen wir Menschen ein selbstbestimmtes Leben in ihrer gewohnten Umgebung.
## Was Sie bei uns erwartet ##
* Sie pflegen ganzheitlich: Sie stellen eine bedarfsgerechte Pflege sicher und unterstützen Menschen dabei, möglichst selbstbestimmt zu Hause zu leben.
* Sie beraten und begleiten: Sie sind für Klientinnen, Klienten und Angehörige eine verlässliche Ansprechperson und schaffen Sicherheit im Alltag.
* Sie übernehmen Verantwortung: Im Bezugspflegesystem können Sie zusätzlich die Fallverantwortung übernehmen und Ihre Fachkompetenz gezielt einsetzen.
* Sie koordinieren die Pflege: Als zentrale Ansprechperson stimmen Sie therapeutische Massnahmen mit dem Behandlungsteam ab.
* Sie arbeiten eigenständig: Ihre Einsätze finden direkt bei den Menschen zu Hause statt. Dadurch erleben Sie Pflege aus einer sehr persönlichen Perspektive.
## Warum es sich für Sie lohnt ##
* Ab 40 % Pensum möglich: Sie können bereits ab einem Teilzeitpensum einsteigen.
* Flexibler Stellenantritt: Sie starten per sofort oder nach Vereinbarung.
* Fachlicher Austausch: Sie arbeiten im Team und über das Team hinaus interprofessionell mit weiteren Fachstellen im Gesundheitswesen zusammen.
* Entwicklung: Sie erhalten Möglichkeiten zur fachlichen Weiterentwicklung und zum individuellen Ausbau Ihrer Kompetenzen.
## Worauf wir bei Ihnen zählen ##
* Ihre Erfahrung: Sie bringen Erfahrung in der ambulanten Pflege mit oder sind interessiert an einem Wechsel in die ambulante Pflege.
* Ihre Haltung: Sie arbeiten gerne mit Menschen und schätzen die Pflege im vertrauten zuhause. Sie sind eine verantwortungsbewusste und empathische Persönlichkeit.
* Ihre Persönlichkeit: Sie arbeiten selbstständig, flexibel und eigeninitiativ.
* Ihre Mobilität: Sie verfügen über einen gültigen Führerausweis und ein eigenes Auto.
## Einblick in unseren Alltag ##
Pflege ist vielseitig. Manchmal herausfordernd. Oft berührend. Und nie langweilig. In unseren Videos zeigen Mitarbeitende, was ihren Pflegealltag ausmacht - fachliche Herausforderungen und wertvolle Begegnungen mit Klientinnen und Klienten.
